macro_actions.name: Engagement and Therapeutic Relationship Building
macro_actions.description: Therapist establishes a genuine, collaborative relationship with the patient characterized by warmth, empathy, openness, and trust, setting the stage for productive dialogue and intervention.

goal.objective: Build a safe and collaborative therapeutic foundation for intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Patient feels understood, safe, trusting, and actively engaged in the therapy process.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient shows some openness and willingness to participate, even if guarded.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient feels misunderstood, unsafe, withdrawn, or resistant to collaboration.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses trust, participates willingly, or positively references the relationship.

states: Initial sessions where rapport must be established
When trust or openness is low or resistance is present
Patient expresses hesitancy, shame, or uncertainty about therapy
Therapeutic progress stalls due to a weak relationship

macro_actions.name: Assessment and Cognitive Case Formulation
macro_actions.description: Therapist gathers information, explores patterns, and synthesizes cognitive, emotional, and behavioral data to collaboratively develop a shared understanding of the patient's difficulties using CBT models.

goal.objective: Create an individualized CBT-based formulation that links theory with the patient’s problems and informs targeted intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient share a clear, collaboratively-built formulation aligned with CBT principles, guiding targets for change.
success_levels.acceptable: Basic understanding of presenting problems and some relevant cognitive patterns are established.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No meaningful formulation is constructed; information remains fragmented or unshared.

goal.reward_hint: Therapist and patient verbalize agreement on a case formulation or identify shared goals based on it.

states: Initial therapy sessions when presenting problems and history are unclear
After rapport is established but targets for intervention have not been identified
Complex or intertwined symptom presentations needing clarification

macro_actions.name: Psychoeducation
macro_actions.description: Therapist provides clear, tailored information about CBT principles, diagnosis, symptom mechanisms, and treatment rationale to foster patient understanding, reduce stigma, and empower self-management.

goal.objective: Improve patient insight and understanding of problems, CBT approach, and rationale for intervention.

success_levels.ideal: Patient accurately understands and can explain CBT concepts relevant to their case, increasing motivation.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient receives relevant information and shows partial understanding or curiosity.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Patient misunderstands or rejects CBT explanations or shows increased confusion.

goal.reward_hint: Patient asks informed questions, discusses new insights, or shows increased engagement following psychoeducation.

states: Beginning phase or with new topics/interventions
When patient displays misconceptions, unrealistic expectations, or confusion about therapy or their symptoms
Following assessment when introducing the CBT model

macro_actions.name: Collaborative Identification of Target Cognitions and Behaviors
macro_actions.description: Therapist and patient jointly identify problem-maintaining thoughts, beliefs, assumptions, and behaviors as focal points for intervention, ensuring relevance and ownership.

goal.objective: Develop a prioritized list of key cognitions and behaviors to target in therapy.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient agree on a clearly defined set of target cognitions/behaviors directly linked to distress or dysfunction.
success_levels.acceptable: Therapist identifies some relevant targets; patient acknowledges their importance.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Targets remain vague or unrelated to the patient’s lived experience.

goal.reward_hint: Agreement and explicit list of priority targets is documented in session.

states: After case formulation, before intervention planning
When specific problematic beliefs or behaviors are evident and require clarification
At points where therapy focus needs realignment

macro_actions.name: Planning and Design of Behavioral Experiments
macro_actions.description: Therapist leads collaborative design of behavioral experiments (BEs) to test specific beliefs/predictions, challenge avoidance, or facilitate new learning, ensuring tailoring to individual needs and capabilities.

goal.objective: Produce a feasible, relevant, and collaboratively agreed upon plan for behavioral experiments to test maladaptive cognitions and promote change.

success_levels.ideal: Therapist and patient have a detailed plan for an experiment addressing critical beliefs, with clear predicted outcomes.
success_levels.acceptable: Experiment is loosely planned with intent to test target cognition, though some details may be missing.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No experiments are planned, or designs are irrelevant, unsafe, or un-agreed upon.

goal.reward_hint: Patient expresses commitment or curiosity about the experiment, and details are clearly identified.

states: Therapy sessions after target beliefs are identified
When patient is ready to move from discussion to experiential learning
Before exposure/interpersonal experiments designed to test avoidance or catastrophic predictions

macro_actions.name: Execution of Behavioral Experiments and Structured Experiences
macro_actions.description: Therapist guides, facilitates, and sometimes models the patient’s participation in planned behavioral experiments or exposure tasks, either in-session or assigned as homework, with attention to safety and relevance.

goal.objective: Successfully engage the patient in the structured experience/experiment to generate direct evidence and learning.

success_levels.ideal: Patient actively participates, experiment proceeds as planned, and meaningful data for hypothesis testing is gathered.
success_levels.acceptable: Experiment is attempted with partial engagement; some learning occurs despite challenges.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Experiment is avoided, disrupted, or leads to adverse outcomes.

goal.reward_hint: Patient’s actions align with the planned experiment and outcome data are available for follow-up.

states: After experiment planning, before reflection or review
Patient is ready and willing to test beliefs ‘in vivo’ or through structured tasks
During exposure-based tasks or skills practice

macro_actions.name: Observation and Data Gathering
macro_actions.description: Therapist and patient observe, record, and collect data on the outcomes of experiments, behaviors, emotional responses, and cognitions as they unfold, ensuring unbiased evidence gathering.

goal.objective: Provide objective data for evaluating the validity of beliefs and intervention effectiveness.

success_levels.ideal: Complete, unbiased observations and data capture relevant to initial predictions.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial data or observations recorded, sufficient for basic hypothesis testing.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No meaningful data gathered; observations are ignored or misinterpreted.

goal.reward_hint: Concrete observation records (written, verbal, behavioral) are available post-experiment.

states: Immediately after experiments or exposure sessions
When hypotheses need empirical data for evaluation
After a meaningful behavioral intervention

macro_actions.name: Reflection and Cognitive Restructuring
macro_actions.description: Therapist facilitates collaborative reflection on experimental outcomes, supports cognitive restructuring, encourages reconsideration of maladaptive beliefs, and fosters integration of new learning into core perspectives.

goal.objective: Modify dysfunctional beliefs and construct more adaptive perspectives based on evidence and reflection.

success_levels.ideal: Patient demonstrates meaningful cognitive change, adopts new adaptive beliefs, and recognizes evidence against old assumptions.
success_levels.acceptable: Partial reconsideration or tentative adoption of alternative perspectives occurs.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Beliefs remain unchanged or become more rigid despite evidence.

goal.reward_hint: Patient verbalizes changed or challenged beliefs and integrates experiment results.

states: After gathering data from behavioral experiments
When evidence contradicts or supports patient’s core beliefs
Following significant emotional or behavioral experiences in therapy

macro_actions.name: Skills Training and Development of Coping Strategies
macro_actions.description: Therapist teaches, models, and reinforces adaptive skills (e.g., assertiveness, emotion regulation, self-monitoring, alternative coping) to address difficulties and enhance patient self-efficacy.

goal.objective: Increase the patient’s repertoire of effective coping and self-management strategies.

success_levels.ideal: Patient acquires and flexibly applies new skills across relevant life domains.
success_levels.acceptable: Patient learns basic skills and uses them in limited contexts.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No skill acquisition or skills not used beyond sessions.

goal.reward_hint: Patient reports or demonstrates use of new coping or behavioral skills outside therapy.

states: When functional or behavioral deficits are identified
Patient expresses a need for practical strategies
Preparation for new behavioral experiments or challenging situations

macro_actions.name: Relapse Prevention and Future Planning
macro_actions.description: Therapist and patient collaboratively develop strategies for relapse prevention, including identifying early warning signs, triggers, and formulating adaptive plans for future setbacks, ensuring maintenance of gains.

goal.objective: Equip patient with individualized plans to sustain change and respond effectively to future challenges.

success_levels.ideal: Clear, collaboratively-developed relapse prevention plan is in place and patient expresses confidence in its use.
success_levels.acceptable: Basic strategies are discussed, and patient shows some awareness of future risks.
success_levels.unsuccessful: No future planning; patient remains vulnerable to relapse with no strategies.

goal.reward_hint: Patient articulates awareness of relapse risks and proactive coping plans.

states: Following substantial progress in therapy
Before planned discharge or therapy ending
Patient expresses concern about setbacks or past relapses
